findings.text: LOOP-1 is not covered: ITER-1 covers restoration of the iteration count (`current_iter=2` → loop starts at iter 2, skipping iter 1 entirely), but no SPEC covers skipping already-complete member stages within the interrupted iteration. If build completed in iter 2 before test was interrupted, build re-runs on resume; nothing in ITER-1's Then or And (or any other SPEC) addresses "which member stage within the interrupted iteration to start from." The dispatch-unit loop's skip guard (SKIP-1) applies to top-level `_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS` entries only; cycle members are dispatched by `_cycle_dispatch` inside the cycle orchestrator, which emits `stage.start` unconditionally for `_cd_iter > 0` with no resume skip. — "resumes at the interrupted stage of that round" [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]
